name: Clef, Clef-Flash, Clef-Omni (decision models)

lineage.base_model: Clef: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B; Clef-Flash: Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B; Clef-Omni: Qwen/Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct
lineage.how_derived: post-trained with a joint schema head (small transformer reading the backbone's final hidden states, routing evidence to each question and scoring all options of all questions jointly)

purpose: Turn a state and a schema of typed questions into decisions with a probability per option in a single forward pass, without free-form generation or output parsing: classification, routing, judging, scoring (card; Cloudflare blog: 'faster, cheaper multimodal').

license.name: Apache-2.0
license.notes: LICENSE read in the Clef repo (Apache License 2.0); the Flash and Omni repos list the same file.

architecture.kind: decision model: standard VLM backbone plus a joint schema head replacing generation; Clef-Omni uses the Qwen3-Omni MoE thinker (30B-A3B) with vision and audio encoders
architecture.why_this_design: card: one forward pass returns probabilities for every allowed option, so there is no generation and no parsing; the blog post that explains the choices was not read

variants.notes: 30B-A3B, adds audio; about 64 GB GPU memory in bfloat16 per the card; includes unused talker/code2wav weights

pc-12gb.notes: 19.1 GB against a VRAM budget of 9.6 GB (VRAM minus about 2.4 GB), KV cache not included; Clef 27B needs 55 GB and Clef-Omni 70.7 GB in BF16, which fits no class

pc-16gb.notes: 19.1 GB against a VRAM budget of 13.6 GB (VRAM minus about 2.4 GB), KV cache not included; Clef 27B needs 55 GB and Clef-Omni 70.7 GB in BF16, which fits no class

pc-24gb.notes: 19.1 GB against a VRAM budget of 21.6 GB (VRAM minus about 2.4 GB), KV cache not included; Clef 27B needs 55 GB and Clef-Omni 70.7 GB in BF16, which fits no class

pc-32gb.notes: 19.1 GB against a VRAM budget of 29.6 GB (VRAM minus about 2.4 GB), KV cache not included; Clef 27B needs 55 GB and Clef-Omni 70.7 GB in BF16, which fits no class

mac-16-24gb.notes: 19.1 GB against a GPU share of about 12 GB (KV cache not included); Clef 27B needs 55 GB and Clef-Omni 70.7 GB in BF16, which fits no class

mac-32gb.notes: 19.1 GB against a GPU share of about 22 GB (KV cache not included); Clef 27B needs 55 GB and Clef-Omni 70.7 GB in BF16, which fits no class

mac-64gb+.notes: 19.1 GB against a GPU share of about 52 GB (KV cache not included); Clef 27B needs 55 GB and Clef-Omni 70.7 GB in BF16, which fits no class

other: transformers with the repo's custom code
engine_support.notes: The head and decision decoding are custom code; no GGUF known.

benchmarks.name: Decision Index 0.2.1 internal run: BFCL case exact accuracy

strengths: A decision model reads a state (text, JSON, images) and a schema of typed questions and returns calibrated probabilities for every option in one forward pass; it does not generate text.
Flash is 38.8 ms per request and beats Clef on most listed benchmarks in the vendor table
weaknesses: not a chat or coding model
weaker than Jev on GPQA Diamond, MMLU-Pro and BBH in the vendor table
best_for: routing, triage, judging and classification steps in an agent pipeline
soft.maturity: Cloudflare release with a public leaderboard (Decision Index); Clef 2.4k likes, 78k downloads; Flash 932 likes; Omni 163 likes

tona_fit.reason: A distinct model class (typed probabilistic decisions), useful as a fast router or judge beside a worker, not as the worker. Clef-Flash at 19 GB BF16 is the only size that fits a consumer class, and no quantization exists yet.
blockers: no generation: needs its own decoding path and an API like SystemOne

open_questions: how the Cloudflare blog explains the schema head and training
independent Decision Index placement of Clef (the community board lists JEV-27B-VL first on vision)
whether a Q4 quantization keeps calibration
